summary: Every LLM request this app builds itself goes through Router: the Anthropic and OpenAI clients that ai_scientist/llm.py hands to every stage are wrapped with the vendored runtime, the reviewer client is built the same way instead of inline, and aider's LiteLLM requests for OpenAI models are routed too. Three trade-offs were needed to make the traffic servable: seed is dropped from Router-bound requests, the review ensemble asks for its five samples one at a time instead of using n=5, and the app's retired model ids (its default claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620 and its hard-coded gpt-4o-2024-05-13 reviewer among them) are mapped to catalog models, which changes which model answers. The OpenRouter llama path, the Gemini path, the Bedrock/Vertex Claude clients and aider's Anthropic path stay where they are, and nothing changes at all until RAMP_ROUTER_API_KEY is set.
reviewed: Looked at model choice per stage, Flex and who waits, prompt caching for the repeated review prompt, the hand-rolled backoff retries, one client vs several, and parallelising the review ensemble; the caching and one-client wins were small enough to fold into the migration itself, and the one improvement worth prototyping (asking the five ensemble samples concurrently to win back the latency the n=5 port cost) was dropped because a live probe showed it degrades spend labels and trips a race in the vendored runtime's policy loading, so it is recorded as a note instead of a branch.

items.title: Route the clients every stage shares
items.summary: The Anthropic and OpenAI clients that create_client() hands to every pipeline stage now send their requests through Router, and each request carries the stage that asked for it.
items.gains: One key and one gateway for idea generation, novelty checks, writeup and review; spend recorded per pipeline stage; the reviewer client is no longer a second, unrouted client built inline
items.why: Every request the app builds itself is made in ai_scientist/llm.py from a client that create_client() returns, so the two first-party clients there are the only places that need wrapping. The runtime translates the app's Chat Completions calls to Responses and keeps anything Router cannot serve on the provider, and it is inactive until RAMP_ROUTER_API_KEY is set. The review stage built its own openai.OpenAI() inline in launch_scientist.py and experimental/launch_oe_scientist.py; those now call create_client() so they are routed like the driver client. Labels: the app knows which stage a request is for only through its call stack (get_response_from_llm takes no stage argument), so llm.py reads the nearest caller outside itself and sends it as x-router-migrate-feature, giving labels like generate_ideas:generate_ideas and perform_review:perform_review instead of one label for the whole app.

evidence.detail: repo suite with Router on against the simulator: 10 passed (4 compileall targets, 6 module imports), same as the base commit

check --run on a probe calling create_client + get_response_from_llm for 8 of the app's models: 6 requests reached router-sim, all valid, each labelled with the calling stage and the client reported as ai_scientist/llm.py:create_client
check --run --live: 4 requests, all 200 - 3 on /v1/responses (provider openai) and 1 on /v1/messages (provider anthropic), labels probe_live:<module> and generate_ideas:generate_ideas, 0.8-1.1 s each

items.title: Drop seed from Router-bound requests
items.summary: The seed=0 that llm.py sends on every OpenAI chat request is removed from the copy that goes to Router, so those requests can be served there.
items.gains: The whole OpenAI path can move; without this every seeded request stayed on the provider
items.loses: The nominal determinism of seed on the OpenAI path. OpenAI only ever documented it as best-effort, these calls sample at temperature 0.75 (0.1 for the reviewer), and nothing in the code reads system_fingerprint.
items.why: Router's Responses API rejects seed with a 400, so the runtime keeps any request carrying it on the provider. router.policy.json drops it from Router-bound requests only: if a request falls back to the provider it still carries seed exactly as the code built it, and the app's own source is unchanged.

evidence.detail: ROUTER_MIGRATE_TRACE on the probe run: the gpt and o1-mini branches show to=chat (routed); before the drop the same sites reported staying on the provider
repo suite with Router on against the simulator: 10 passed

items.title: Ask the review ensemble one sample at a time
items.summary: The five-reviewer ensemble asks for five separate samples instead of one request with n=5, and the repeated prompt is given a cache key.
items.gains: The review ensemble - the step launch_scientist always runs with num_reviews_ensemble=5 - moves to Router; the five identical prefixes now share a prompt cache key, so the provider can serve them from its prompt cache (cache reads cost $0.1 vs $0.4 per 1M on gpt-4.1-mini)
items.loses: Input tokens are billed per sample instead of once per ensemble (up to 5x the paper-length prompt, less whatever the prompt cache absorbs), and the five samples are sequential, so the review step takes about 5x as long. Nobody waits: the review runs at the end of an unattended pipeline that has just spent hours on experiments and a writeup.
items.price: gpt-4.1-mini $0.4/$1.6 per 1M, cache reads $0.1 per 1M; no model change here
items.why: The Responses API Router serves has no n, so the runtime kept n=5 requests on the provider. The gpt/llama branch of get_batch_responses_from_llm now loops get_response_from_llm, exactly what the branch for every other model already did, so each request is n=1. The returned shape is unchanged - a list of n contents and a list of n message histories - which is what perform_review reads when it averages the ensemble's scores and rewrites msg_history.

evidence.detail: check --run on get_batch_responses_from_llm(n_responses=3): 3 valid /v1/responses requests, and the function returned 3 responses and 3 histories as before
check --run --live with n_responses=2: 2 requests, both 200 on gpt-4.1-mini, 1.1 s for the pair, both answers returned in order
repo suite with Router on against the simulator: 10 passed

items.title: Map retired model ids to catalog models
items.summary: The model ids the app offers that Router no longer lists - including its default Claude model and its hard-coded reviewer model - are mapped to catalog models on Router-bound requests.
items.gains: The default path moves at all: of the 40 ids in AVAILABLE_LLMS the catalog serves only gpt-4o-mini and gpt-4.1-mini, so without this the app's default --model (claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620) and its reviewer (gpt-4o-2024-05-13) both stayed on the provider, and the ids Router listed a generation ago (gpt-4o, o1) cost a 404 round-trip first. Also cheaper per token on most paths: gpt-4o $2.5/$10 to gpt-4.1-mini $0.4/$1.6, o1 $15/$60 to gpt-5.1 $1.25/$10.
items.loses: Answers will differ: a different model generation writes the ideas, the experiment notes, the paper text and the reviews. On the o1/o3 branch the app caps output at 4096 tokens, which a current reasoning model can spend on reasoning before answering (the same risk the app already runs on o1 itself). gpt-4.1-nano runs now get gpt-4o-mini, so those two menu entries become the same model.
items.price: claude-3-5-sonnet-* to claude-sonnet-4-5: $3/$15, unchanged. gpt-4o*/gpt-4.1* to gpt-4.1-mini: $2.5/$10 to $0.4/$1.6. gpt-4.1-nano* to gpt-4o-mini: $0.15/$0.6. o1* to gpt-5.1: $15/$60 to $1.25/$10. o1-mini*/o3-mini* to gpt-5-mini: $0.25/$2. deepseek-chat/-coder to deepseek-v4-flash: $0.13/$0.26. deepseek-reasoner to deepseek-v4.1-flash: $0.3/$1.2.
items.why: Targets are chosen to keep the request shape the code builds working: models that still accept temperature, because the ensemble relies on it for diversity (claude-sonnet-4-5 rather than claude-sonnet-5, which rejects temperature), and, on the non-reasoning branches, models that will not spend the app's 4096-token output cap on reasoning (gpt-4.1-mini rather than a gpt-5 mini). DeepSeek keeps its vendor, and this is also what activates the api.deepseek.com unlock from m1, so reverting this commit sends the DeepSeek calls back to api.deepseek.com. The map lives in router.policy.json and applies to Router-bound requests only, so a provider fallback still asks for the id the code chose.

evidence.detail: check --run --live: claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620 returned 200 from /v1/messages served by claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 (provider anthropic), and gpt-4o-2024-05-13 returned 200 served by gpt-4.1-mini (provider openai)

check --run over 8 of the app's models: requests arrive as gpt-4.1-mini, gpt-4o-mini, gpt-5-mini, deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4.1-flash, all valid; llama3.1-405b and gemini-1.5-flash never reach Router
targets and prices read from the live catalog via router-migrate levers on 2026-10-14; every target is temperature-capable except gpt-5-mini, whose branch sends temperature=1 that the runtime drops

a paper-review comparison of gpt-4o-2024-05-13 against gpt-4.1-mini needs full papers through both models, which the spend cap and the time budget did not allow; the reviewer should treat the review quality of gpt-4.1-mini as unverified

items.title: Route aider's OpenAI traffic
items.summary: The coder that writes the experiments and the paper sends its OpenAI-model requests through Router as well.
items.gains: The largest part of a run's spend - aider rewriting the experiment code run after run, then the LaTeX - is on Router for OpenAI-model runs, under the same key as the rest
items.loses: nothing, and it does not cover everything: aider's Anthropic requests go through LiteLLM's own Anthropic handler rather than an OpenAI SDK client, so a run with the default Claude model keeps its coder traffic on Anthropic (see n1)
items.price: no change beyond the model map in m4
items.why: aider calls models through LiteLLM, which builds its OpenAI SDK clients on litellm.client_session, so installing the runtime's transport there routes those requests. route_aider_through_router() is called at import time in the three entry points that build a Coder, so the worker processes launch_scientist spawns install it too, and it is a no-op without RAMP_ROUTER_API_KEY.

evidence.detail: check --run on a probe that imports launch_scientist and then calls litellm.completion for gpt-4o-mini: 1 valid /v1/responses request, client reported as ai_scientist/llm.py:route_aider_through_router; the same probe's claude-3-5-sonnet request went to api.anthropic.com instead
repo suite with Router on against the simulator: 10 passed, launch_scientist and perform_writeup still import cleanly with the install at module scope

items.title: Llama 3.1 405B keeps its OpenRouter path
items.summary: Runs with --model llama3.1-405b keep calling OpenRouter directly.
items.gains: nothing: the capability is kept as it is
items.why: Router's catalog has no Llama id at all, so there is nothing to map this call to that would still be the model the user asked for. The client keeps the user's OPENROUTER_API_KEY and its openrouter.ai base URL; a probe confirms no request from this branch reaches Router.

evidence.detail: check --run: the llama branch's request was blocked as openrouter.ai traffic (by design) and appears in no Router log
router-migrate levers, live catalog 2026-10-14: 68 ids, none of them a Llama model

items.title: Gemini runs keep Google's endpoint
items.summary: Runs with a Gemini model keep calling Google's OpenAI-compatible endpoint with the user's own key.
items.gains: nothing: the capability is kept as it is
items.why: None of the Gemini ids the app offers (1.5, 2.0, 2.5-preview) is in Router's catalog, and the Gemini ids Router does list are Vertex entries that require a provider credential held by the Router account - Router returns 403 provider_key_required otherwise - so they cannot be served with the GEMINI_API_KEY this client is built from. The client is therefore left unwrapped. The scanner reports this site as routing; that is a false positive, it reads the request site without seeing which client reaches it.

evidence.detail: check --run: the gemini branch's request was blocked as generativelanguage.googleapis.com traffic and never appears in the Router log or the runtime trace

items.title: Aider's Claude runs still bypass Router
items.summary: On the default Claude model, aider's coder traffic - most of a run's tokens - still goes straight to Anthropic.
items.gains: Routing it would put the biggest spender in the app on Router for the configuration the README recommends
items.loses: nothing is lost today; the traffic simply stays on Anthropic
items.price: unknown until a route is chosen
items.why: LiteLLM serves Anthropic through its own HTTP handler, not an OpenAI SDK client, so the runtime's litellm install does not reach it (measured: a probe's gpt-4o-mini request routed, its claude-3-5-sonnet request went to api.anthropic.com). The ways round it all have a cost a human should weigh: point aider at an OpenAI-model id so it uses the routed path, pass aider an OpenAI-compatible base URL on Router (aider's Claude prompt and edit-format tuning then applies to a model reached as an OpenAI endpoint), or patch LiteLLM's Anthropic handler, which is editing a dependency's internals. The experiment loop is the product, so none of these should be chosen without a full run to compare against.

evidence.detail: check --run on the litellm probe: gpt-4o-mini reached router-sim as a valid request; claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620 was blocked as api.anthropic.com traffic, i.e. it stayed on the provider

items.title: Parallel review samples not taken
items.summary: Asking the five ensemble samples at the same time would win back the latency m3 cost, but a live probe showed it loses spend labels and trips a race in the runtime.
items.gains: would restore the single-request wall clock of the old n=5 review ensemble
items.loses: per-stage spend labels on those requests, and some of the samples silently fall back to the provider
items.why: A prototype ran the five samples in a thread pool. Two things went wrong and both are worth knowing before anyone tries again: the stage label is derived from the call stack, and inside a worker thread there is no application frame to find, so the requests were labelled ai_scientist/llm.py:get_response_from_llm instead of the calling stage; and a live probe of five concurrent samples had two of them fall back to the provider with reason "model is not in the Router catalog", because the vendored runtime loads the compiled policy (which holds the model map) lazily without a lock, so a thread can read it half-initialised. Single-threaded code is unaffected, and launch_scientist's --parallel uses separate processes, so the migration as committed does not hit this. The prototype branch was deleted rather than proposed.

evidence.detail: check --run --live on a 5-sample concurrent ensemble: 3 requests reached Router (all 200), the other 2 went to api.openai.com and failed on the dummy provider key

same probe offline with ROUTER_MIGRATE_TRACE: 2 of the entries read to=provider, reason "model 'gpt-4o-2024-05-13' is not in the Router catalog", i.e. the policy's model map was not yet visible to those threads

items.title: Claude path is broken before any request
items.summary: The installed Anthropic SDK no longer accepts temperature on messages.create, so Claude runs raise a TypeError independently of Router.
items.why: ai_scientist/llm.py passes temperature= to client.messages.create, and anthropic 1.13.0 (the version installed here) has moved it out of that signature, so the call fails before any HTTP request. This is pre-existing at the base commit and nothing in this migration touches it; it is left as it is because fixing it means changing what the app sends. It is recorded because it is why the Claude evidence above comes from a probe that builds the same request without temperature rather than from get_response_from_llm.

evidence.detail: probe through get_response_from_llm with claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620: TypeError "Messages.create() got an unexpected keyword argument 'temperature'"; inspect.signature on anthropic 1.13.0 confirms temperature is gone from messages.create
